For the preparation-stage reading sequence, use [solver observations](course/solver-observations.qmd). This page owns what a Palace run records about the quality of its mesh.

## What `mesh()` audits {#audit}

`mesh()` meshes the SGB model with `scgsim.meshing`, which audits every
tetrahedron of each round's mesh. The measure is the minimum signed inverse
condition number (minSICN) of each element, taken on the linear mesh before
any elevation to the geometry order. Every tetrahedron must reach the mesh's
`quality_threshold` (default `0.01`); elements below it are refined in the next
round of the repair loop, within the budgets of
[Palace mesh controls](specs/palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#palace-mesh-controls).
A mesh that cannot be brought to the threshold stops `mesh()`, and no
`palace.msh` is delivered. The sizes the audited mesh starts from, including
those at film walls and on Surface-EPR band boundary curves, are the sizing
recipe's ([Sizing recipes](specs/palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#palace-mesh-recipes)).

The threshold is the meshing module's acceptance check for a valid element. It
is not a scientific acceptance gate: convergence of a result is read from the
solver's own outputs.

## The quality report {#quality-report}

Each run writes the report to the run's `mesh/` folder as JSON
(`<model>.quality.json`) and as a short text summary (`<model>.quality.txt`).
The mesh manifest records the report's path and SHA-256.

::: {.askr-table-compact}
| Field | Records |
|---|---|
| `quality_measure`, `threshold` | `minSICN` and the threshold the run was held to. |
| `stop`, `rounds`, `history` | How the repair loop ended and what each round changed. |
| `mesh` | Tetrahedron and node counts, `min_quality`, `bad_count` below the threshold, `measured_on` (`linear mesh before elevation`), the delivered `geometry_order` and the 3D algorithm. `null` when no round produced a mesh. |
| `remaining_bad`, `stop_places` | The elements still below the threshold, with location, groups and feature kinds, and where they cluster in micrometres with the fine edges or faces found there. Empty for a clean stop. |
| `recipe`, `repair`, `mesher`, `budgets`, `time_budget` | The settings the run used. |
| `timing` | Total, per-round, meshing and audit seconds. Kept under one key, so two runs of the same input compare equal without it. |
:::

minSICN is measured before elevation, so the report does not describe curved
high-order elements of the delivered `palace.msh`. The manifest records the
order and the native element types of the mesh that was written.

## Edge statistics {#edge-statistics}

The Palace
[mesh summary](specs/palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#mesh-manifest-and-detached-summary)
records each physical region's unique primary-corner edge count and minimum,
mean, and maximum straight chord lengths in micrometres. These remain chords on
curved high-order elements; they are not curved arc lengths or a higher-order
quality metric. Point regions have zero edges and no length extrema. Missing
historical statistics remain `not_recorded`.

## Version identities of a mesh {#version-identities}

A mesh that `mesh()` writes carries three versions. Read them to tell whether
two meshes were made the same way.

::: {.askr-table-compact}
| Identity | Example | Where it is recorded | When it changes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Package version | `scgsim 3.0.0rc1` | `scgsim_version` in the run's provenance (`metadata/route_b_provenance.json`, or `route_a_…` on Route A) | With every release of SCGSim. |
| Recipe version | `scgsim.meshing.features/N` for `FeatureRecipe`, `scgsim.meshing.uniform-boundary/N` for `UniformBoundaryRecipe`, `scgsim.meshing.global-size/N` for `GlobalSizeRecipe` | `recipe.version` in each quality report and in the mesh manifest, beside `recipe.parameters` | Only when the sizes the recipe asks for change. |
| Report format | `scgsim.meshing.report/N` | `report_version` in each quality report | When the fields of the quality report change. |
:::

A recipe's version goes up only when the sizes it asks for change. `FeatureRecipe`
went from `features/1` to `features/2` when it began to size every Surface-EPR
band boundary curve. So two reports with the same recipe version and the same
parameters asked for the same initial sizes, even when they were made by
different package releases; a different recipe version means the meshes were
made by different sizing rules. The recipe version covers the initial sizes
only: the repair policy is recorded in each report, and the Gmsh version in the
mesh manifest.

The versions are separate because one version for the whole meshing module
would change whenever any recipe changed, and could not say which one did. A
run with `UniformBoundaryRecipe` keeps its version when `FeatureRecipe` changes,
so its reports stay comparable across that change.

For example, the same default `FeatureRecipe()` on a flip-chip qubit with bands
of 0.5 and 1 µm (the OrcaPen SC PDK `disk_flip_chip_qubit` under common ground
planes, Route B) gives two different meshes under the two versions:

::: {.askr-table-compact}
| | `scgsim.meshing.features/1` | `scgsim.meshing.features/2` |
|---|---|---|
| Sizes asked for | 1.30 µm on the 801 film-wall curves | 1.30 µm on 3,104 curves: the film walls and every band boundary curve |
| First mesh | 402,784 tetrahedra, 1 below the quality threshold | 569,325 tetrahedra, none below it |
| Result | clean after one repair round: 407,093 tetrahedra, 82.5 s | clean in the first mesh: 569,325 tetrahedra, 53.4 s |
:::

The two quality reports name different recipe versions, so the different mesh
comes from the sizing rules, not from anything else in the run.
